title: The salt that named the city
description: A short film from inside the salt mine in the Dürrnberg, above Hallein, south of the city, mined since the Celts. Salt paid for Salzburg’s cathedral and palaces, and gave the city its name, “salt castle.”

title: A fortress that was never taken
episode: A Guided Tour through Hohensalzburg Fortress in Salzburg, Austria
description: A short tour from the fortress itself. Begun in 1077 and enlarged by the prince-archbishops who ruled Salzburg, it is one of the largest medieval castles in Europe, and no enemy ever captured it.

title: An archbishop’s practical jokes
episode: Austria's 400-year-old gravity fountains still work perfectly
description: Archbishop Markus Sittikus built Hellbrunn as a summer palace around 1615, with trick fountains that soak unsuspecting guests. They still run on water piped from the hills, with no pumps.

title: Mozart and the archbishop
episode: Mozart Snapshot #8: Mozart in the Home of the Prince Archbishop
description: Pianist Katie Mahan plays and talks in the Residenz, where the young Mozart performed for Salzburg’s ruler. Mozart worked for Archbishop Colloredo until 1781, when he quit and was, in his words, kicked out the door.

title: The carol, filmed in 1953
episode: SILENT NIGHT: THE STORY OF THE CHRISTMAS CAROL  1953 EDUCATIONAL FILM AUSTRIA XD
description: An educational film from 1953 that tells the story of “Silent Night,” first sung on Christmas Eve 1818 in Oberndorf, north of Salzburg. The church was later torn down after floods, and a small chapel stands in its place.

title: Why the chocolate balls are named for Mozart
episode: Why These Chocolate Balls Are Named After Famous Composer Mozart | Tasty Legacies
description: The Mozartkugel, pistachio marzipan and nougat dipped in dark chocolate, was invented in 1890 by the confectioner Paul Fürst. His family still makes them by hand in this café and sells them in silver foil.

title: The festival’s first century
episode: 100 years of Salzburg Festival. A journey through history.
description: The festival’s own short history, from the first performance of Everyman in 1920 through the Nazi years to the opera and concert festival of today. Its halls are built into the cliff of the Mönchsberg.

title: Everyman on the cathedral steps
episode: Hugo von Hofmannsthal: Everyman (Jedermann) Salzburg Festival 2020
description: A trailer for Everyman, Hugo von Hofmannsthal’s morality play about a rich man summoned by Death. It has opened the festival on the square in front of the cathedral almost every summer since 1920.

title: Karajan at the festival in 1963
episode: Karajan at the Salzburg Festival 1963 (Documentary | English Subtitles)
description: A short 1963 documentary of conductor Herbert von Karajan at work at the festival. Karajan, born in Salzburg in 1908, dominated the festival for decades and founded its Easter festival in 1967.

title: The real story behind the film
description: A promotional short made for The Sound of Music in 1965, touring the Salzburg locations used in the film. The children sang “Do-Re-Mi” around the fountains and steps of the Mirabell Gardens.

title: Beer in a monastery hall
episode: Rainer Herbe, Augustiner Bräu Kloster Mülln, Salzburg Beer Culture
description: Austria’s largest beer hall, in a former monastery in Mülln where monks began brewing in 1621. You take a stone mug from the shelf, rinse it, and have it filled from a wooden barrel.

title: A dessert shaped like the hills
episode: Why Salzburger Nockerln are so hard to make
description: Salzburger Nockerl is a sweet soufflé baked in three peaks, said to stand for the city’s hills, with powdered sugar for snow. It has to be eaten the moment it leaves the oven, before it falls.
